why: A ⇒ B fails for two genuine reasons. (1) B assumes only AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak (f ≢ 0), but A needs AdmitsBumpFunctions (f(x) ≠ 0), and the project has only strong ⇒ weak. (2) B reads 'an associated open neighbourhood U' universally: for EVERY open U ⊇ S_f with S_{f+s} compact for all s ∈ Γ^{+,1}_U, there is a good s ∈ Γ^{+,1}_U. A (theorem_5_25, universes 0) only gives SOME such U, the one its proof builds from properness via Theorem 5.18, and says nothing about sections supported in a prescribed U. With both points removed (strong bumps, ∃ U), A ⇒ BExStrong is proved: A_to_BExStrong, #rt_check OK. There, good position is taken from A, and the sub-M-polyfold and HasCornerStructure come from SolutionSetInGeneralPosition. B ⇒ A fails, also genuinely. B assumes IsTameStrongBundle Bd (an equivalent strong bundle atlas whose base retractions are all tame). A has only PX.IsTame plus tame germ data (germ reading, as in B), i.e. one tame chart near each smooth point, not an atlas. Also, A's conclusion SolutionSetInGeneralPosition is far more than B's 'good position + corner structure': it adds transversality, GENERAL position at every zero, S_{f+s} a compact smooth submanifold in general position, tameness, and d_S = d_X.
B_issue: Not a bug, but two reading choices that decide A ⇒ B. 'Bump functions' is read as AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak (the project uses f(x) ≠ 0). 'An associated open neighbourhood U' is read as an arbitrary U with the compactness property, so the claim is made for every such U; the text probably means the U produced by properness/Theorem 5.5. B also adds a tame strong bundle hypothesis.
